# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh from `titan help`. Do not edit by hand. -->

```text
OVERVIEW: Reproducible per-project Linux dev environments on your Mac, in lightweight VMs.

Every project gets its own Linux VM, defined by a standard devcontainer.json and pinned by
titan.lock, so "works on my machine" means works on every machine. Your editor and files stay on
the Mac; commands run in the VM.

Get started:
  mkdir shop && cd shop
  titan create node        set up this folder (node, python, go, rust, ruby, java)
  npm run dev              commands run in the project's VM

Docs: https://github.com/manoj1604/titan

USAGE: titan <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

START SUBCOMMANDS:
  create                  Set up this folder as a Titan project and start its VM.

WORK IN A PROJECT SUBCOMMANDS:
  up                      Create or start this project's VM.
  down                    Stop the project's VM and its services (--rm deletes them; data is kept).
  run                     Run a command inside the project's VM (starting it if needed).
  shell                   Open an interactive shell inside the project's VM.

SERVICES AND SHARING SUBCOMMANDS:
  add                     Add services (postgres, redis, or any image) to this project.
  share                   Share the project's app on a public HTTPS address (Cloudflare tunnel).
  logs                    Show a service's logs (e.g. Postgres), or the VM's boot log.

CHECK AND CLEAN UP SUBCOMMANDS:
  status                  Show this project's VM: state, live CPU and memory, ports, services
                          (--all: every VM on this Mac).
  doctor                  Check that this Mac and project are ready.
  gc                      Delete images that no Titan project or VM needs any more.

  See 'titan help <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

## titan create

```text
OVERVIEW: Set up this folder as a Titan project and start its VM.

Run it in your project's folder (an empty one, or existing code). Titan detects the language from
your files, or uses the one you name, writes .devcontainer/devcontainer.json and starts the VM. The
first time on this Mac it also sets Titan up (container service, shell, VS Code, coding agents).

Examples:
  mkdir shop && cd shop && titan create node    then e.g.  npm create vite@latest .
  cd my-api && titan create                     existing code: detected
  titan create python@3.13 --with postgres

USAGE: titan create [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [<stack>] [--with <with> ...]

ARGUMENTS:
  <stack>                 Language for an empty folder: node, python, go, rust, ruby, java
                          (optionally @version).

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --with <with>           Services, e.g. --with postgres redis.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan up

```text
OVERVIEW: Create or start this project's VM.

USAGE: titan up [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [--rebuild]

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --rebuild               Recreate the VM from scratch.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan down

```text
OVERVIEW: Stop the project's VM and its services (--rm deletes them; data is kept).

USAGE: titan down [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [--rm] [--volumes]

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --rm                    Delete the VMs instead of just stopping them (service data is kept).
  --volumes               Also delete service data (databases). Implies --rm.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan run

```text
OVERVIEW: Run a command inside the project's VM (starting it if needed).

Arguments after `--` go to the command unchanged. The VM starts (or is set up) if needed; paths
inside the project are mapped into the VM, and the exit code is passed back.

Example:
  titan run -- npm test

USAGE: titan run [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [--root] [<command> ...]

ARGUMENTS:
  <command>               Command and arguments.

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --root                  Run as root (for projects that use their own user).
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan shell

```text
OVERVIEW: Open an interactive shell inside the project's VM.

You get a Linux prompt in your project folder; type `exit` to come back to the Mac (the VM keeps
running). Commands run as root unless the project sets `customizations.titan.user` (e.g. "me" for
your own user with sudo); then --root opens a root shell.

USAGE: titan shell [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [<target>] [--root] [--or-mac]

ARGUMENTS:
  <target>                Project or VM to enter, from any folder: a project name (shop), VM name,
                          service (shop/postgres) or path. Default: the current folder's project.

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --root                  Open a root shell (for projects that use their own user).
  --or-mac                Outside a Titan project (or if the VM can't start), open your normal Mac
                          shell instead. Used by VS Code's Titan terminal profile.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan add

```text
OVERVIEW: Add services (postgres, redis, or any image) to this project.

Each service runs in its own VM, reachable from the app by its name (e.g. `postgres`), with its
data on a volume that survives `titan up --rebuild`. Presets set DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL for the
app.

Examples:
  titan add postgres redis
  titan add postgres:15

USAGE: titan add [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] <services> ...

ARGUMENTS:
  <services>              Presets (postgres, redis) or images.

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan share

```text
OVERVIEW: Share the project's app on a public HTTPS address (Cloudflare tunnel).

By default you get a random *.trycloudflare.com link that lasts while the command runs. With your
own domain on Cloudflare, --domain gives a stable address that never changes; Titan remembers it
for the project. Needs cloudflared (brew install cloudflared).

Examples:
  titan share                        quick link, until Ctrl-C
  titan share -b --ttl 2h            in the background; closes after 2 hours
  titan share --protect              visitors need a password
  titan share 5173 8000              one link per port
  titan share --domain dev.example.com --always
  titan share --list | --stop | --log

USAGE: titan share [<options>] [<ports> ...]

ARGUMENTS:
  <ports>                 Ports to share, as the app sees them (default: the first forwarded port).

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  -b, --background        Keep running after this terminal closes.
  --ttl <ttl>             Close the tunnel after this long (e.g. 30m, 2h, 1d).
  --protect               Ask visitors for a password (Titan makes one up).
  --password <password>   Ask visitors for this password.
  --domain <domain>       Your hostname on a Cloudflare domain, for a stable address (remembered
                          for this project).
  --always                With a domain: bring the tunnel up whenever this project's VM starts.
  --forget                Forget the remembered domain for these ports.
  --list                  List the tunnels running on this Mac.
  --json                  With --list: machine-readable output.
  --stop                  Stop this project's tunnels (or only the given ports).
  --log                   Follow the visit log: who is using the link.
  --copy                  Copy the link to the clipboard.
  --keep-host             Pass the public hostname through instead of rewriting Host to localhost.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan logs

```text
OVERVIEW: Show a service's logs (e.g. Postgres), or the VM's boot log.

Your app's own output goes to the terminal where you started it (e.g. `npm run dev`); visits to a
shared link are in `titan share --log`.

Examples:
  titan logs postgres          everything so far
  titan logs postgres -f       follow live (Ctrl-C to stop)
  titan logs redis -n 50       the last 50 lines
  titan logs --boot            the project VM's boot log (when it won't start)

USAGE: titan logs [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [<service>] [--follow] [-n <n>] [--boot]

ARGUMENTS:
  <service>               Service name (default: the project's only service).

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  -f, --follow            Keep following new lines.
  -n <n>                  Show only the last N lines.
  --boot                  Show the boot log instead of the output.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan status

```text
OVERVIEW: Show this project's VM: state, live CPU and memory, ports, services (--all: every VM on
this Mac).

USAGE: titan status [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [--all] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  -a, --all               List every Titan VM on this Mac.
  --json                  Machine-readable output (for scripts and coding agents).
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```

## titan gc

```text
OVERVIEW: Delete images that no Titan project or VM needs any more.

Keeps images used by any VM and images pinned or used by projects you've run `titan up` in. By
default only images Titan pulled or built are removed; --all also removes other unused images.
Unused shared toolchains are removed too. Asks before deleting.

USAGE: titan gc [--directory <directory>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] [--all] [--cache] [--yes]

OPTIONS:
  -C, --directory <directory>
                          Run as if titan was started in <dir>.
  -v, --verbose           Show debug output.
  --dry-run               Print the container commands instead of running them.
  --all                   Also remove unused images Titan didn't create.
  --cache                 Also empty the package cache shared by all VMs (npm, pip, Go modules).
  -y, --yes               Don't ask for confirmation.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

```
